thesis: India's AI/data-centre buildout creates a multi-year capex chain: land & shells -> power generation/transmission -> transformers/switchgear/gensets -> cooling -> cables/fibre/networking -> servers/GPU compute. As of August 2026 the demand side is no longer in doubt - Cummins reports data centres at 40% of powergen revenue, Blue Star booked Rs1,500 cr of DC MEP orders in one quarter, Hitachi Energy named 560 MVA + 800 MVA of DC transformer orders, and L&T won a Rs10,000-15,000 cr NVIDIA B300 AI Factory contract. Two things have changed the shape of the thesis. First, POWER is the binding constraint, not land: the government's own AI data-centre load estimate DOUBLED to 26.3 GW by FY32 (from 13.56 GW in March 2026), while facilities build in 12-18 months against 3-5 years for grid. Second, the August 2026 share-price move was triggered by a US trade action - a DRAFT FCC ban on Chinese optical transceivers - not by India demand, which means much of this basket is now levered to US policy follow-through it does not control.
method_note: Per SECTOR_INTELLIGENCE_FRAMEWORK.md: evidence is temporal and decays. Every evidence item is dated; order-win items have a half-life of roughly 1-3 weeks (interpretation) to quarters (earnings/guidance), while structural items (capacity plans, policy) last years. Exposure ratings are categorical states, not scores. Nothing here is a fair-value model - it is the L1 evidence layer for an AI-infra hypothesis set. The 12-month grade added on 2026-08-13 deliberately stores its THREE INPUTS separately (evidence quality, exposure purity, how much is priced in) rather than combining them into a number, because the framework's own rule is 'explicit categorical states + evidence, not invented scores'.

hypotheses.text: The August 2026 India AI-infra rally was triggered by a US TRADE action, not by India demand or policy
supporting: On 4 August 2026 Reuters reported the FCC is preparing an import ban on Chinese optical transceiver modules for US data centres; US optical names ripped (AAOI +20%, Coherent +18%, Lumentum +14%)
On 5 August STLTECH and HFCL each hit 5% upper circuits, explicitly attributed to those proposed curbs

The Nifty went nowhere over the same period (24,570 on 7 Aug to 24,436 on 12 Aug) - this was a stock-specific move, not an index re-rating
contradicting: Q1 FY27 results were genuinely strong across the basket and several prints (Black Box, TD Power, Hitachi Energy, Finolex) landed inside the window with real order-book evidence
Smallcaps outperformed broadly (+2.7% in the 3-7 Aug week), so some of the move is a size effect rather than a theme effect
hypotheses.note: THE MEASURE IS STILL A DRAFT. No final FCC order, implementation schedule or product definition has been published; target implementation is before end-2026. If it is dropped, the August catalyst disappears.
